Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
207 PM PDT Tue Oct 13 2026

.SYNOPSIS...13/206 PM.

A Santa Ana wind pattern will create much warmer temperatures 
this week as well as gusty northeast winds at times, strongest 
Thursday and Friday. Another significant cool down is likely
into next week.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-FRI)...13/206 PM.

HIGH CONFIDENCE in a MODERATE TO STRONG SANTA ANA event peaking 
this Thursday and Friday with damaging wind, power outages and
large fast moving fires possible in the region. HIGH WIND 
WATCHES, Wind Advisories and Red Flag Warnings cover the typical 
Santa Ana Wind Corridor in Los Angeles to Ventura County for 
Thursday and Friday. A Fire Weather Watch is also in effect Friday
for the Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo interior mountains. A 
Heat Advisory is also in effect Thursday through Saturday for 
Coastal areas with highs up to 95 degrees. See weather.gov/lox to 
view individual product details.

Some actions to consider with the upcoming wind/heat/fire weather
hazards: 

Have a plan in place in the case of a power outage, especially if
a wind or fire weather product is in effect in your area.

Secure loose outdoor items and be prepare for dangerous cross
winds when driving, especially on elevated roadways.

In the event of a nearby wildfire, smoke may increase heat and
physical stress. If smoke impacts your area; 1) Have a cooling plan
in place as smoke could limit your ability to cool your home through
open windows and 2) If you have air conditioning, set on air
recirculation within the home to avoid smoke exposure. Local
officials may have additional guidance.

Forecast details:
The forecast through this weekend remains largely unchanged. A 
low pressure system is moving slowly through the Great Basin 
through Wednesday. That will set the stage for a developing Santa 
Ana wind event across portions of southern California this week as
high pressure over the Great Basin forces winds up and over the 
mountains and down into the valleys and coastal areas. The rapid 
acceleration of the air into increasingly higher pressure at lower
elevations will force the air to heat up significantly (per the 
gas law). Will start to see this process as early as today as the 
upper low advances to the southeast, allowing the transport of air
from the north to begin. Latest models show just a very light 
north-northeast wind developing over the mountains today and 
tonight, then increasing in speeds each day through Friday, by 
which time winds aloft will be around 40-50 mph. In response, 
temperatures across the coast and valleys will warm by roughly 10 
degrees each day, peaking Friday with highs in the upper 80s to 
mid 90s in most areas. Mountains and deserts will warm as well but
by much lower amounts.

The Santa Ana winds will be strongest for most areas Friday but 
Thursday likely a close second within the Santa Wind Corridor of
Los Angeles to Ventura Counties. We could see wind gusts into the
60s and 70s in the most favored exposed areas of the San Gabriel 
Mountains. Widespread peak gusts of 35-55 mph are expected within
the Wind Advisory. Gusty east winds of 30-40 mph may expand into
interior Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo mountains into Friday
and is covered by the Fire Weather Watch.

.LONG TERM (SAT-TUE)...13/206 PM.

One more day of gusty Santa Ana winds are possible (30-40 percent
chance of reaching advisory levels) into Saturday, taking on a
more easterly orientation.

Temperatures are expected to remain well above normal through 
Sunday, but rapidly cool into early next week. And looking out a 
little further there is fairly high agreement in the models that 
another cold upper low will move into the area the middle of next 
week, for another big swing into temperatures and weather 
conditions. It looks like mainly a dry system at this point, but 
there is a 30-40 percent chance that it tracks just enough 
offshore to support some shower activity. The much cooler weather
will arrive on gusty northwest to west winds focused in the
Tuesday/Wednesday window.

&&

.AVIATION...13/1804Z.

At 1736Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor inversion.

High confidence in TAFs.

KLAX...High confidence in TAF. Any E wind component expected to
remain below 7 kt.

KBUR...High confidence in TAF.

&&

.MARINE...13/107 PM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current
forecast. For the afternoon and evening periods through Wednesday,
there is a 40-60% chance of SCA level winds around Point 
Conception. For Thursday through Saturday, high confidence in 
winds and seas remaining below SCA levels for most of the waters.
The only exception is there is a 20-30% chance of E-NE SCA level
wind gusts across the outer waters south of the Channel Islands
and west to northwest of San Nicholas Island due to Santa Ana
winds during the late night through morning hours Thursday through
Saturday. The highest chances are on Friday.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Through Wednesday, there is a 30%
chance of SCA level winds in the afternoon and evening hours. 
Otherwise expect conds to remain below SCA levels. 

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate 
confidence in current forecast. Through Wednesday, high 
confidence in winds and seas remaining below SCA levels for most 
area, but the only exception is the western half of the Santa 
Barbara Channel where there is a 50% chance of SCA level winds 
this afternoon and evening. Thursday through Saturday, there is a
40-60% chance of SCA level northeast winds from Ventura south to 
Santa Monica and out past Anacapa Island and possibly from the
Orange County Coast out to Catalina Island, strongest during the 
late night into early afternoon hours.

Long period swells from the west and the south are affecting the
coastal waters, and can create a confused sea state. This can 
make boating more challenging and dangerous, especially for small 
vessels.

&&

.BEACHES...13/105 PM.

While the peak timing for the most impactful coastal flooding has
passed, there is still a threat of minor coastal flooding, mainly
minor tidal overflow, into Thursday afternoon due to continued 
high tides and elevated surf. The highest tides will occur during 
the mornings and range from 6.5 to 7.0 feet, with secondary high 
tides during the evening (around 5 feet). As for elevated surf, a 
long period southerly swell and long period westerly swell will 
impact the coastal waters the next several days.

A Beach Hazards Statement is in effect into Thursday afternoon for
the LA/Ventura County Beaches. 

Please continue to monitor the forecast and refer to the Coastal 
Hazard Product (CFWLOX) for more information.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...13/1019 AM.

Offshore flow will steadily increase each day through Thursday or
Friday, then weaken over the weekend. During the Thursday and 
Friday peak, northeast winds of 20 to 40 mph with gusts to 40 to 
60 mph will be common over the wind prone areas of Los Angeles and
Ventura Counties, with localized gusts of 60 to 70 mph in the 
mountains. Interior Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo Counties 
will also see east winds which peak on Friday of 15 to 25 mph with
gusts of 30 to 40 mph. Meanwhile, the air will rapidly warm and 
dry. Minimum humidities will generally lower into the 5 to 15 
percent range by Friday, with poor overnight recoveries starting 
Thursday. This will greatly dry out any affects of the recent
rains. All of this will add up to a high risk for large fires and
rapid fire growth, with Red Flag conditions likely for most of 
Los Angeles and Ventura Counties Thursday through Friday. There 
is also a moderate risk for Red Flag conditions over interior 
Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo Counties on Friday. Cooler and 
improved conditions likely next week.

&&
